subject: Banded discount structure for new Real-time Insights workload
messages:
From: Emma Lin <emma.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial pricing convo - Real-time Insights

Ben — thanks for the overview in the demo earlier. The product team loved the latency profile; we do have a few follow-ups about economics before we move to procurement:

1) Our Real-time Insights product is highly bursty (daily peaks 200x baseline). We need clarity on how banded per-token discounts would apply when traffic spikes. Is there a smoothing/grace period?
2) We may start with a small committed monthly spend for Q3 and expand teams in Q4. Can you outline incremental commit credits vs. straight per-token discount?
3) Any minimum duration or minimum spend for a tier change?

Attaching a simple traffic sample and a short procurement checklist. If possible, can we get a revised quote that shows: baseline per-token price, band thresholds, and the pricing if we add a second product line mid-quarter?

Best,
Emma Lin
Head of Product — Nimbus Analytics

---
Attachments: traffic-sample.csv (csv), procurement-checklist.docx (docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: initial pricing convo - Real-time Insights

Emma — appreciated the great questions. Quick answers up front, then I included a proposal summary and next steps:

1) Banded discounts and burst smoothing: we offer a banded discount schedule (0-50M tokens, 50-200M, 200M+) for hosted API usage. For bursty traffic we can apply a 72-hour rolling window to average peak usage when evaluating tier placement, which prevents a single short spike from permanently escalating you to the next tier. We can shorten that window for committed customers by agreement.

2) Incremental commits vs per-token: two common paths — a) usage-only with banded per-token discounts (no minimum commit), b) committed credits (monthly commit) that yield an up-front % credit and lower unit pricing. Incremental commits (e.g., add $X/month mid-term) are pro-rated for the remainder of the billing period and count toward the next period's tier calculation.

3) Minimum duration: for commit discounts we generally have a 3-month minimum for small pilot commits and 12-month for enterprise reserved tiers. We can be flexible for strategic pilots.

Attached is a short exhibit showing three scenarios: pure usage with bands, a $30k/month incremental commit, and a path to a $120k/quarter reserved tier if you add the second product. Key ask: can you share expected monthly token volume for baseline and peak for Q3 so I can produce the numeric quote?

Proposed next step: 30-min call early next week to walk the numeric scenarios and confirm procurement needs.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redwood-pricing-exhibit-rev2.pdf (pdf), nimble-commit-scenarios.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Emma Lin <emma.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: initial pricing convo - Real-time Insights

Thanks Ben — I uploaded our Q3 monthly token estimate to the Drive link you provided (folder: Nimbus -> Redwood RFP). High level: baseline ~40M tokens/mo, expected daily peak days push to ~800M tokens on event days (2–3 days/mo). For the second product (scheduled for Oct) we estimate additional baseline of 15M tokens/mo with similar peak patterns but lower amplitude.

Procurement flagged three items: audit logs retention (12 months), SOC 2 evidence, and a shortened notice period for increasing tiers (we prefer 7 days). Can you confirm Redwood's position on each?

I can do a call Monday 10am PT if that works for you.

—Emma

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: initial pricing convo - Real-time Insights (proposal + DocuSign)

Emma — thanks for the traffic numbers, very helpful. I ran the scenarios with our pricing team and attached a short quote that shows explicit math for your baseline and two peak days. Highlights:

• Option A — Usage-only (banded): baseline unit $0.0048/token for 0–50M, $0.0039 for 50–200M, $0.0031 for 200M+. With 72-hour smoothing, estimated monthly bill (Q3 baseline) ~$192k.
• Option B — Incremental commit ($30k/mo): reduces baseline unit to $0.0038 and provides $30k in monthly credits pro-rated. Peaks are still billed but the rolling window reduces tier hops. Estimated monthly net ~$150k.
• Option C — 12-month reserved path (goal: $120k/quarter commit): lowers unit to $0.0026 and includes priority capacity for scheduled peak days; requires 90-day notice for tier decreases.

Procurement items: audit logs retention — yes, 12 months available (enterprise add-on). SOC 2 evidence — we will provide the current report; Neha will attach the evidence PDF once signed off. Notice period — we can accept 7-day increase notices for tier escalation; decreases from committed reserved tiers are subject to the minimum durations noted.

Next steps:
1) Emma to confirm preferred option (A/B/C).
2) If B or C, Procurement to confirm PO cadence and signatory.
3) We'll send a DocuSign for the selected exhibit — preview link included.

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/orm/example-sign/12345
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HS-83421

Can we confirm Monday 2pm PT to finalize? I included Marissa from Commercial Ops to help with contractual language if needed.

Thanks,
Ben

---
Attachments: redwood-pricing-exhibit-rev2.pdf (pdf)

From: Procurement <procurement@nimbusanalytics.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: initial pricing convo - Real-time Insights (proposal + DocuSign)

Ben / Neha — procurement here. Quick confirmation: Nimbus prefers Option B (incremental commit) with the following clarifications before we sign:

• Pro-rating for mid-cycle increment must be applied at an hourly granularity for burst credits (we have very short spike windows).
• SLA: we require a 99.9% availability SLA for the committed reserved capacity days.
• We need SOC 2 report and encryption-at-rest confirmation attached to the agreement.

We can route the PO once those items are included. We'll plan for a 30-day payment term. Please attach the revised exhibit to the DocuSign packet and we'll aim to get signatures by end of week.

Procurement — Nimbus Analytics
